source_text: Si igitur - inquio - non nisi per sexum fetus, non nisi per corpus sexus, non nisi per Deum corpus; quis ambigat fecunditatem Deo iure reputari? Hoc tam certum est, ut etiam tua in suam laudem ora concusserit. Verum post praeconium huic a te loco redditum, haeresim admones introduci, cum ea quae subdidi, nihil aliud quam quae praemissa fuerant, admota explanatione geminaverint.
pass_a_gloss: If therefore — I say — the offspring is not except through sex, sex not except through a body, a body not except through God, who would doubt that fertility is rightly credited to God? This is so certain that it even struck your mouth into its own praise. But after the proclamation rendered by you to this place, you warn that heresy is being introduced, although those things which I subjoined doubled nothing other than what had been set forth beforehand, an explanation having been applied.
pass_b_english: “If, then,” I say, “offspring come only through sex, sex only through a body, and a body only through God, who could doubt that fertility is rightly attributed to God?” This is so certain that it forced even your mouth to praise it. But after paying this passage your tribute, you warn that a heresy is being introduced, although the words I added merely repeated what had come before, with an explanation attached.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
